Vs
Arvind Mahajan and another ..... Respondent(s)
 Through: Mr. Sunil Sethi, Sr. Advocate

with
 Mr. Ravi Abrol, Advocate.

Coram: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE RAHUL BHARTI, JUDGE  ORDER (05.06.2024)
1.
The court of Principal District Judge, Reasi came to dispose of a land acquisition reference on file No. 11/Ref of 2008 by virtue of an award dated 28.09.2013.

2. Said reference was sought by late Satish Mahajan, ex proprietor/owner of the land acquired by the Collector Land Acquisition, Northern Railways, Udhampur for the public purpose sought by the indenting department, Northern Railways, Udhampur.

3. Said award dated 28.09.2013 left both that is the Collector Land Acquisition and the legal representatives of Satish Mahajan aggrieved who have come forward with statutory appeal under the Land Acquisition Act, Svt. 1990 in the form of CFA No. 46/2013 instituted on 27.12.2013.

sentences.text: 1 4. In this memo of appeal, the authorities came to be named as the respondents are the Collector Land Acquisition, Northern Railways Udhampur and the Deputy Chief Engineer S & C-III Northern Railways, Udhampur.

5. As against the appeal so filed by the legal representatives of the original owner of the acquired land Mr. Satish Mahajan, the Collector Land Acquisition, Northern Railways, Udhampur also stepped forward with an appeal to challenge the award dated 28.09.2013 so passed by the court of District Judge, Reasi on reference file No. 11/Ref of 2008.

6. The institution of this statutory appeal by the Collector Land Acquisition, Northern Railways,
Udhampur came to take place on 14.03.2016 beyond the period of limitation prescribed for maintaining an appeal against an award under the J&K Land Acquisition Act, Svt. 1990 by the court of District Judge, Reasi deciding a reference under section 18 of the said Act.

7. Thus, the said time barred appeal came to accompanied with an application of condonation of delay CONC No. 38/2016 supported by an affidavit of the then Collector Land Acquisition, Northern Railways, Udhampur.

8. In the said time barred appeal, the Collector Land Acquisition, Northern Railways, Udhampur impleaded the son and widow of late Satish Mahajan as the respondents No. 1 & 2 to be contesting respondents and the Deputy Chief Engineer S & C-III Northern Railways, Udhampur as proforma respondent, being the indenting authority.
c/w 9.

In this application for condonation of delay, on behalf of the proforma respondent-Deputy Chief Engineer S & C-III Northern Railways, Udhampur, Mr. P. S. Chandel, Advocate came to cause appearance in terms of an order dated 12.07.2019 and came to register no objection to the condonation of delay application filed by the Collector Land Acquisition, Northern Railway,
Udhampur with respect to the time barred appeal.
10. The delay attending the filing of the appeal by the Collector Land Acquisition, Northern Railways, Udhampur against said award dated 28.09.2013 is of 804 days.

11. While this condonation application was pending adjudication, the proforma respondent-Deputy Chief Engineer S & C-III Northern Railways, Udhampur came to prefer an application CM No.
4618/2022, thereby seeking his transposition to be co-applicant and co-appellant in the time barred appeal.

12. In the application seeking transposition as co-applicant and co- appellant with the Collector Land Acquisition, Northern Railways, Udhampur, the proforma respondent-Deputy Chief Engineer S & C-III Northern Railways, Udhampur came to state that since Northern Railways is the indenting department being the transferee of the land acquired and for payment of compensation bearing the liability to pay the same, as such, it also requires to be on the side of the Collector Land Acquisition,

2 Northern Railways, Udhampur so as to be co-applicant and co-appellant.
13.

entities.text: Collector Land Acquisition, Northern Railways, Udhampur
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: CM No. 4618/2022 came to be filed on 01.08.2022.

Thus, in essence two applicants are now seeking condonation of delay for the purpose of c/w maintainability and entertainment of the statutory appeal against the award dated 28.09.2013 passed by the court of District Judge, Reasi on file No. 11/Ref of 2008.
14.

In the name of showing cause for the delay what has been stated in the application is reproduced herein as under:
"2.

That the appeal above titled could not be filed within the prescribed time as the papers concerning the case had to pass through various echelons of the official hierarchy and at each level the matter required time consuming consideration.
3. That the matter finally reached the law department which give its sanction for filing the appeal on 10.03.2016 after studying entire pros and cons of the judgment."

15. Thus, by the force of averments as made in the para-2 & 3, the Collector Land Acquisition,
Northern Railways, Udhampur joined by the Deputy Chief Engineer S & C-III Northern Railways,
Udhampur are meaning to explain the delay of this much number of 804 days.

16. Even if this Court were to act to the expectation of a lax approach in condoning the delay still the averments made in the Para-2 & 3 of the application would fall short of providing a cause, much less a sufficient cause, to explain the delay of 804 days because what the two applicants are meaning to plead before this Court is that there is an echelon of official hierarchy through which the papers of the concerned case have to pass through and at each level the matter requires time consuming consideration before finally reaching the Law Department which gives its sanction for filing of an appeal and, c/w accordingly, in this case the appeal came to be presented on 10.06.2012 after studying the entire pros and cons of the judgment.

17. It is the Collector Land Acquisition, Northern Railways, Udhampur who has come up with fancy of his own mind that for the purpose of filing the appeal, the papers had to pass through various levels of official hierarchy and each level, the time consumed but without annexing even a single piece of paper or citing even a single date or event as to when the said process came to set into effect and how lasted before each level of the official hierarchy.
By filing such a frivolous application, the Collector Land Acquisition, Northern Railways, Udhampur has exhibited gross callousness on his part in the matter of handling legal matters.

18. The tone and tenor of the said two paragraphs mean to say as if the framers of the law of limitation were ignorant of the understanding of functioning at the government level and therefore,
while engrafting section 5 of the Limitation Act were oblivious of the fact that the court related judgments amenable to appeals have to pass through various echelon of the official hierarchy and that every level of that hierarchy, a time consumption is an inevitable fact and, therefore, in the matter of government and its officials, the law of limitation shall be held to be relaxed to the utmost Collector Land Acquisition vs Arvind Mahajan And Another on 5 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123811946/
3 level.
19.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Article 14 of the Constitution of India creates equality before laws and government, or for that matter government officials/authorities, are no exception to that article.
What is the sufficient cause has nothing to do with whether it is attending a case of a person, natural or juristic, government or any other body.

Thus, in the name of the said two paragraphs, the applicants are meaning to plead frivolity expecting this Court to act mechanically in condoning the delay and letting the appeal to be adjudicated on merits.

21. This Court is not meant to be taken for a ride by the applicants, and therefore, finds that the application filed by two applicants, one original and other one transposed, as frivolous having consumed the time of this Court lasting upto 8 years.
22. CONC No. 38/2016 is, accordingly, dismissed.
23. Let this appeal come up for its adjudication on 20.07.2024.
(RAHUL BHARTI) JUDGE JAMMU 05.06.2024
